items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: I remember one time you played a parade with Joe H. Lewis, you know, and the crowd was talking about, you know.

ctx.x: Well, there aren't many clarinet players called Kit, are they? That's mostly trumpet players. No, no clarinet players. No.

The only one that called himself Kit was Wayne Smolga. Yeah. At least he had a sense of humor. Well, like, Kid Ari is a trauma-in-law, doesn't it? Kid Avery, Joe Avery. And Kid Williams, A. Well, anyway. But I never can recall a clarinet play doing that except for the moment of all. Kid Ernest. Well, I've heard people call you the clarinet wizard. You know? Yeah. I'd hear them say that in the street. I remember one time you played a parade with Joe H. Lewis, you know, and the crowd was talking about, you know. He…
With that? With two clarinets and then one dance band? Yeah. Piku would double, but he'd use the saxophone. One guy would play high register, one guy low, or play the same thing, or what?
